games.name: Castlevania: The Adventure
games.summary: The first Castlevania game for the Game Boy, following Christopher Belmont as he battles through four grueling stages to defeat the immortal Count Dracula. Armed with only his whip and a handful of sub-weapons, Christopher must navigate treacherous platforming sections filled with classic Castlevania enemies. Despite its technical limitations on the handheld hardware, the game successfully captures the gothic atmosphere and punishing difficulty that defines the series.
games.additional_summary: A stripped-down but atmospheric entry in the Castlevania series, featuring the iconic whip-based combat and gothic environments. The game is known for its slow pace compared to nes entries.
games.trivia: Christopher Belmont is Simon Belmont's ancestor, set 100 years before the original Castlevania. The game was criticized for its sluggish movement speed.

games.name: Super Mario Advance 2: Super Mario World
games.summary: A faithful and feature-rich port of the legendary Super Nintendo launch title Super Mario World, Super Mario Advance 2 brings the entire Dinosaur Land adventure to the Game Boy Advance with Mario and Luigi both fully playable for the first time in the classic game. Players traverse nine sprawling worlds packed with 96 exits to discover, rideable Yoshis of multiple colors with distinct abilities, and an enormous variety of stage types ranging from ghost houses and castles to underwater caverns and sky fortresses. The GBA version adds voiced character exclamations, a Luigi mode with altered physics, and the ability to save progress at any point — making it the definitive portable version of one of the greatest platformers ever created.
games.additional_summary: Super Mario World is widely considered the peak of 2D Mario game design, and this GBA port preserves everything that made it a masterpiece while adding quality-of-life improvements and a fully playable Luigi with his floatier, higher-jumping moveset.
games.trivia: Super Mario World was the best-selling SNES game of all time, shipping over 20 million copies. Yoshi, who debuted in this game, was originally conceived during development of the original Super Mario Bros. but was cut due to hardware limitations.

games.name: Kirby's Dream Land 2
games.summary: Kirby returns to the Game Boy in a greatly expanded sequel, teaming up with three lovable animal friends — Rick the Hamster, Kine the Fish, and Coo the Owl — to recover the Rainbow Bridges stolen by the shadowy villain Dark Matter. Each animal companion fundamentally changes how Kirby's copy abilities work, adding immense depth and variety to the gameplay across seven colorful worlds. The game introduced one of Kirby's most iconic recurring antagonists and set the template for future entries in the series.
games.additional_summary: A major step up from the original Dream Land, this sequel introduced Kirby's signature copy abilities to the Game Boy along with animal companions that change how each ability works.
games.trivia: This was the first Game Boy Kirby game to include copy abilities. Dark Matter, who debuted here, went on to become a recurring villain in the Kirby series.

games.name: Doom
games.summary: Doom for the Game Boy Advance is a port of id Software's legendary 1993 first-person shooter, bringing the iconic demon-blasting action to Nintendo's 32-bit handheld. Players take on the role of a space marine fighting through 24 maze-like levels across the Martian moon base, battling hellspawn with an arsenal of chainguns, plasma rifles, and rocket launchers.
games.additional_summary: The port is based on the Atari Jaguar version of Doom, sharing its simplified map geometry and reduced monster roster — notably absent are the Cyberdemon and Spider Mastermind. The game was censored to obtain a Teen rating from the ESRB, replacing red blood with green. It uniquely includes eight exclusive deathmatch-only levels not found on any other platform, playable via the Game Link Cable with up to four players. A static lighting option was added to boost performance on the GBA dim first-generation screen.
games.trivia: Doom on GBA was the first portable console port of the game and remains the only official release of Doom to include exclusive multiplayer-only deathmatch levels. The game soundtrack, handled by audio director Allister Brimble, suffered from known synchronization issues caused by a code error during the transfer from the Jaguar codebase. Speedrunners discovered an out-of-bounds glitch in late 2017 that allows the entire game to be completed in under 10 minutes.

games.name: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening
games.summary: After a violent storm shipwrecks him on the mysterious Koholint Island, Link must collect eight magical Instruments of the Sirens hidden across sprawling dungeons in order to wake the sleeping Wind Fish and find his way back home. The game features a surprisingly emotional and philosophical narrative, inventive dungeon design, and unexpected cameos from the Mario universe that delighted players worldwide. Widely regarded as one of the greatest handheld games ever made, it was later lovingly remade for the Nintendo Switch in 2019.
games.additional_summary: One of the most beloved Zelda games ever made, Link's Awakening features a deeply emotional story, clever dungeons, and surprising cameos from Mario characters. It was later remade for Nintendo Switch in 2019.
games.trivia: Link's Awakening was originally developed as an unofficial side project by Nintendo staff. It was the first Zelda game not set in Hyrule and not featuring Princess Zelda as a character.

games.name: Mega Man V
games.summary: In the fifth and final Game Boy Mega Man adventure, the Blue Bomber faces an entirely new threat — the Stardroids, a group of powerful alien robots themed after the planets of the solar system who have arrived to conquer Earth. Mega Man is equipped with a brand new Mega Arm weapon that replaces the classic Mega Buster, adding a punch-and-grab mechanic that can be powered up throughout the game. Featuring fully original bosses, a unique upgrade system, and tight gameplay, it is universally considered the pinnacle of the Game Boy Mega Man series.
games.additional_summary: Unlike the other Game Boy Mega Man titles which reused bosses from the nes games, Mega Man V features entirely original bosses themed around planets in the solar system. It is widely considered the best Game Boy Mega Man entry.
games.trivia: Mega Man V is the rarest and most expensive of the Game Boy Mega Man games. The Mega Arm replaces the Mega Buster and can be powered up over time.

games.name: Metroid II: Return of Samus
games.summary: Intergalactic bounty hunter Samus Aran is dispatched on a solo mission to the remote Metroid homeworld of SR388, tasked with hunting down and eliminating the remaining Metroid population before they can be weaponized by the Space Pirates. The game introduces multiple evolved forms of the Metroid creature and expands Samus's arsenal significantly, rewarding exploration across a sprawling underground world. Despite the Game Boy's monochrome display, the game creates a uniquely isolated and atmospheric experience that laid crucial groundwork for the entire Metroid franchise.
games.additional_summary: A landmark game in the Metroidvania genre, Metroid II expands Samus's abilities and introduces multiple Metroid evolution forms. The game has a haunting atmosphere despite the Game Boy's monochrome display.
games.trivia: Metroid II was remade as Metroid: Samus Returns for the 3DS in 2017. The baby Metroid that hatches at the end of this game is the same one that appears in Super Metroid.

games.name: Pokemon Red Version
games.summary: The game that sparked a worldwide phenomenon, Pokemon Red invites players to embark on a coming-of-age journey across the Kanto region as a young Trainer aiming to catch all 151 Pokemon, defeat eight gym leaders, and ultimately claim the title of Pokemon Champion. Beneath its simple and charming premise lies a surprisingly deep battle system, a rich world full of secrets, and a revolutionary link cable trading and battling feature that made it one of the most social gaming experiences of its era.
games.additional_summary: The game that started a global phenomenon. Pokemon Red and Blue introduced 151 Pokemon, turn-based battles, and a link cable trading/battling system.
games.trivia: Pokemon Red and Green were the original Japanese releases; Blue was a special edition.

games.name: Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3
games.summary: In this bold spin-off from the Super Mario Land series, the greedy antihero Wario stars in his very own adventure, storming through the pirate-infested Kitchen Island to steal the legendary Mamu statue and amass enough treasure to buy a castle grander than Mario's.
games.additional_summary: The game that established Wario as a standalone character, shifting focus from saving a princess to accumulating wealth.
games.trivia: This was the first game where Wario was a playable protagonist rather than a villain.

games.name: Battletoads & Double Dragon
games.summary: An epic crossover brawler that brings together the hard-hitting Battletoads with the legendary martial arts duo Billy and Jimmy Lee from Double Dragon to face the combined threat of the Dark Queen and the Shadow Boss.
games.additional_summary: Features both solo and co-op multiplayer for up to two players simultaneously.
games.trivia: The crossover was initiated by Tradewest, who owned the rights to both franchises at the time.

games.name: Castlevania
games.summary: The legendary gothic action-platformer that launched one of gaming's most iconic franchises, placing players in the boots of vampire hunter Simon Belmont as he whips his way through six haunting stages of Dracula's ominous castle.
games.additional_summary: The game's iconic soundtrack composed by Kinuyo Yamashita is widely regarded as some of the greatest video game music ever composed.
games.trivia: Castlevania was originally released in Japan as Akumajo Dracula. Simon Belmont's design was inspired by Indiana Jones.

games.name: Contra
games.summary: One of the defining games of the nes era, Contra is a ferocious run-and-gun action game following elite commandos Bill Rizer and Lance Bean as they blast through jungles, bases, and alien strongholds.
games.additional_summary: The Konami Code, first popularized by Contra, has since appeared in dozens of games and cultural references.
games.trivia: The main characters Bill and Lance were visually inspired by Arnold Schwarzenegger and Sylvester Stallone.

games.name: DuckTales
games.summary: Based on the beloved Disney animated series, DuckTales follows the world's richest duck Scrooge McDuck as he bounces his iconic cane across five exotic locations in search of five legendary treasures.
games.additional_summary: The game was remastered in 2013 by WayForward Technologies as DuckTales: Remastered.
games.trivia: The Moon stage theme, composed by Hiroshige Tezuka, is widely considered one of the greatest video game music tracks ever written.

games.name: Mega Bomberman
games.summary: Mega Bomberman brings the beloved franchise to the Sega Mega Drive, challenging players to strategically plant bombs, clear enemies, and battle friends in explosive multiplayer mayhem.
games.additional_summary: Mega Bomberman was one of the standout multiplayer titles on the Mega Drive, supporting up to 5 players with the Sega Multitap. Its Battle Mode became legendary at gatherings and is considered one of the best party games on the platform.
games.trivia: The game supports up to 5 players simultaneously using the 4-Way Play / Multitap accessory — a rare feature for its time that made it a go-to couch multiplayer experience.

games.name: Kirby's Adventure
games.summary: One of the most technically impressive nes games ever made, Kirby's Adventure introduced the pink puffball's iconic copy ability mechanic across seven colorful worlds in Dream Land.
games.additional_summary: Kirby's Adventure was one of the last major first-party nes releases and featured a battery-backed save system.
games.trivia: The game was later remade as Kirby: Nightmare in Dream Land for the Game Boy Advance in 2002.

games.name: Super Mario Bros.
games.summary: The game that defined a generation, Super Mario Bros. follows Mario through eight worlds of the Mushroom Kingdom to rescue Princess Peach from the villainous Bowser.
games.additional_summary: Super Mario Bros. was a pack-in title with the NES in North America and is widely credited with revitalizing the video game industry after the 1983 crash.
games.trivia: The clouds and bushes in the game are actually the same sprite, just recolored — a clever trick to save memory on the NES cartridge.

games.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
games.summary: Sonic the Hedgehog is a 2D side-scrolling platformer for the Sega Genesis. Players control Sonic on a mission to stop Dr. Robotnik from enslaving animals.
games.additional_summary: The game introduced iconic gameplay mechanics such as loop-de-loops and speed boosters.
games.trivia: Sonic original concept design had him with fangs and a human girlfriend named Madonna, both scrapped before release.

games.name: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3
games.summary: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 is the updated version of Mortal Kombat 3, featuring an expanded roster of fighters, new stages, and additional finishing moves.
games.additional_summary: The Genesis port brought back fan-favourite characters like Kitana, Jade, and Reptile that were absent in the original MK3.
games.trivia: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 was the first game in the series to introduce the Aggressor bar.

games.name: Ristar
games.summary: Ristar is a 2D action platformer in which players control Ristar, a young star with extendable arms, on a quest to rescue his father.
games.additional_summary: Ristar core mechanic revolves around grabbing enemies with his stretchy arms.
games.trivia: Ristar originated from early concept sketches that eventually evolved into Sonic the Hedgehog.

games.name: Rocket Knight Adventures
games.summary: Rocket Knight Adventures follows Sparkster, a valiant opossum knight with a rocket-propelled jetpack, battling through five worlds to stop the evil pig army.
games.additional_summary: Praised for outstanding production values and set pieces that pushed the Genesis hardware impressively.
games.trivia: The game spawned two sequels — Sparkster on both the Genesis and SNES in 1994.

games.name: One Piece: The Legend of the Wild Sea
games.summary: Based on the massively popular manga and anime series, this GBA title puts players in the straw hat of Monkey D. Luffy battling through iconic enemies and locations.
games.additional_summary: The game draws from early arcs of the One Piece manga.
games.trivia: One Piece was originally rejected by Shonen Jump editors before becoming the best-selling manga of all time.

games.name: Need for Speed: Most Wanted
games.summary: The GBA adaptation follows a young racer working their way up the Blacklist while evading police in the city of Rockport.
games.additional_summary: The GBA version uses a top-down perspective retaining the core Blacklist progression system.
games.trivia: Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005) is widely regarded as the peak of the classic NFS era.

games.name: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
games.summary: The GBA adaptation puts players in the night-vision goggles of Third Echelon operative Sam Fisher across covert missions spanning global hotspots.
games.additional_summary: The GBA version cleverly adapts 3D stealth gameplay into a 2D side-scrolling format.
games.trivia: The original Splinter Cell was heavily influenced by the Metal Gear Solid series.

games.name: Pac-Man Collection
games.summary: Pac-Man Collection bundles four classic Namco arcade titles into a single GBA cartridge.
games.additional_summary: The collection includes faithful ports of all four arcade originals.
games.trivia: Pac-Man, originally called Puck Man in Japan, was renamed for Western markets.

games.name: Dragon Ball Z: The Legend of Goku
games.summary: Dragon Ball Z: The Legend of Goku adapts the iconic Saiyan, Frieza, and Cell sagas into a top-down action RPG.
games.additional_summary: The game covers three major sagas spanning many of the series most memorable moments.
games.trivia: Followed by two GBA sequels — Legacy of Goku II in 2003 and Buu's Fury in 2004.

games.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
games.summary: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 introduces Miles Tails Prower as Sonic's sidekick. Players race through new zones to stop Dr. Robotnik from building the Death Egg.
games.additional_summary: The game introduced the spin dash move and featured the first two-player split-screen competitive mode.
games.trivia: Sonic 2 was developed simultaneously across offices in Japan and the US.

games.name: Road Rash 3
games.summary: Road Rash 3 is an illegal street racing game where players compete in motorcycle races across real-world locations including Kenya, Germany, Brazil, Japan, and the USA.
games.additional_summary: The third entry expanded the global setting significantly and introduced new weapon types.
games.trivia: Road Rash 3 was one of the few EA titles that saw release exclusively on Sega platforms.

games.name: Dragon Ball Z
games.summary: Dragon Ball Z for the Sega Genesis is a fighting game. Players choose from a roster of Z Fighters and villains using energy-based special attacks and melee combat.
games.additional_summary: The game captures the over-the-top power scaling of the anime with screen-filling ki blasts.
games.trivia: Several Dragon Ball Z games were released on the Sega Genesis in Japan under different subtitles.

games.name: WWF WrestleMania: The Arcade Game
games.summary: WWF WrestleMania: The Arcade Game is an over-the-top wrestling brawler featuring real WWF superstars including Bret Hart, Shawn Michaels, Razor Ramon, and The Undertaker.
games.additional_summary: Developed by Midway using digitized character sprites similar to Mortal Kombat.
games.trivia: The game used the same digitization technology as Mortal Kombat to capture the likenesses of real WWF wrestlers.

games.name: Sonic & Knuckles
games.summary: Sonic & Knuckles serves as both a standalone game and the second half of Sonic the Hedgehog 3.
games.additional_summary: The cartridge featured the revolutionary Lock-On Technology slot on top.
games.trivia: Sonic & Knuckles and Sonic 3 were originally intended to be a single game.

games.name: Aladdin
games.summary: Disney's Aladdin for the Sega Genesis is an action platformer based on the 1992 animated film.
games.additional_summary: The Genesis version is widely regarded as the superior port due to its fluid Disney animation.
games.trivia: Aladdin on Genesis was one of the first games to feature animation directly produced by Disney animators.

games.name: Mortal Kombat
games.summary: The handheld port of the arcade phenomenon, Mortal Kombat brings brutal one-on-one fighting to the Game Boy with seven iconic warriors competing in a deadly tournament.
games.additional_summary: The Game Boy version omits the infamous fatalities and blood due to Nintendo content policies.
games.trivia: Mortal Kombat's graphic violence directly led to the creation of the ESRB rating system in 1994.

games.name: The Legend of Zelda
games.summary: The game that defined the action-adventure genre, The Legend of Zelda drops Link into the vast land of Hyrule on a quest to collect the eight pieces of the Triforce of Wisdom.
games.additional_summary: The Legend of Zelda was one of the first nes games to feature a battery-backed save system.
games.trivia: The game's name comes from Princess Zelda, who was named after Zelda Fitzgerald.

games.name: Mega Man 3
games.summary: The third entry in Capcom's Blue Bomber series introduces eight new Robot Masters, the trusty robotic dog Rush, and the mysterious Proto Man.
games.additional_summary: Mega Man 3 was the first game in the series to introduce Rush the robotic dog.
games.trivia: Proto Man was originally intended to appear in Mega Man 2 but was held back for the third game.

games.name: Mega Man 2
games.summary: Universally regarded as one of the greatest video games ever made, Mega Man 2 refined and perfected every element of the original with eight brilliantly designed Robot Masters.
games.additional_summary: Mega Man 2 was a passion project developed after the modest success of the original.
games.trivia: Metal Blade is widely considered the most overpowered weapon in Mega Man history.

games.name: Ninja Gaiden
games.summary: Ninja Gaiden follows the young ninja Ryu Hayabusa as he travels to America to avenge his father's death and uncovers a vast demonic conspiracy.
games.additional_summary: Ninja Gaiden was one of the first nes games to use cinematic cutscenes to advance its story.
games.trivia: The game is notorious for its final boss gauntlet that forces players to re-fight the last three bosses.

games.name: Punch-Out!!
games.summary: Punch-Out!! puts players in the corner of Little Mac as he punches, ducks, and dodges his way up the World Video Boxing Association circuit.
games.additional_summary: The original nes release featured real boxer Mike Tyson as the final boss.
games.trivia: Little Mac is only 17 years old and 107 pounds in the game's lore.

games.name: Super Mario Bros. 3
games.summary: Super Mario Bros. 3 sent Mario and Luigi on an epic quest across eight enormous worlds to rescue seven kings and ultimately save Princess Peach.
games.additional_summary: Super Mario Bros. 3 famously appeared in the 1989 film The Wizard before its North American release.
games.trivia: The game sold 17 million copies worldwide.

games.name: Super Mario Bros. 2
games.summary: Super Mario Bros. 2 takes Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, and Toad to the dream world of Subcon to defeat the evil frog king Wart.
games.additional_summary: Many enemies introduced in Super Mario Bros. 2 became recurring characters throughout the entire Mario franchise.
games.trivia: The original Japanese Super Mario Bros. 2 was considered too difficult for Western audiences.

games.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
games.summary: The first console TMNT game lets players switch between Leonardo, Donatello, Michelangelo, and Raphael battling through Manhattan's streets and sewers.
games.additional_summary: The game is infamous for its third stage electrified underwater dam section.
games.trivia: Despite being a Konami game, this title is notably different from the acclaimed Turtles arcade game.

games.name: Tetris
games.summary: Tetris challenges players to arrange falling Tetrominoes into complete horizontal lines on the NES.
games.additional_summary: The nes version of Tetris gained renewed cultural attention through competitive tournaments.
games.trivia: Nintendo ultimately secured the Tetris rights and bundled it with the Game Boy.

games.name: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
games.summary: Zelda II takes Link on a journey across a vast overworld map to restore six crystals to the palaces of Hyrule and awaken the sleeping Princess Zelda.
games.additional_summary: Zelda II is the only mainline Zelda game to feature a traditional RPG experience point and leveling system.
games.trivia: The sleeping Princess Zelda in this game is an ancestor cursed by a wizard long ago.
